data.cultural_impact: The name Hodge was most prominently used in New England, England, and America during the Middle Ages and Early Modern Period. It was a common name among farmers, laborers, and artisans who understood the importance of a hard-working and god-centered life. The name Hodge also gained popularity through the character Ebenezer Hodge in Nathaniel Hawthorne's short story "The Maypole of Merrymount", where he represented traditional New England Puritan values.
